helper_contract.contract: list_copy_range(dest_base, dest_header, src_first, src_header): deep-copy the source node range [src_first, src_header) -- for each source node, in order, allocate a fresh 0x18-byte node with operator new, copy the source node's +0x10 payload qword into the new node, and append it to the destination list whose header is dest_header; then add the number of copied nodes to the qword at dest_base + 0x10. The source list is not modified; an empty range changes nothing. At this routine's two call sites dest_base == dest_header (the object base for list 1 at 0x5f128b5, object + 0x18 for list 2 at 0x5f12924), so the count that grows is that list's own count field. The contract was read from the helper's observable behaviour at its call sites; in the packet's differential the helper is stubbed with this contract on both sides, which is exactly the claim boundary.

rdi = destination + 0x18, rsi = destination + 0x18 (list-2 header), rdx = current source list-2 node, rcx = source + 0x18 (list-2 header)

landing_pad.target_block: 0x5f127f6 (shared cleanup, no FDE of its own): with rbx = destination object and r12 = destination + 0x18 held from this routine, it operator-deletes (size 0x18 each, no unhook) every node then linked in the destination list 2, then every node then linked in the destination list 1, then calls _Unwind_Resume with the exception object from the pad. The only calls in the body that can throw are the two helper calls (the helper allocates); the delete loop's PLT calls are the noexcept _M_unhook and operator delete. Exception behaviour is pinned at this level only; the model and the differential cover non-throwing runs.

phases.detail: list-1 header self-linked (+0x00 = +0x08 = destination), list-1 count +0x10 = 0, dword +0x30 copied from source +0x30, list-2 count +0x28 = 0, qword +0x38 copied from source +0x38, dword +0x40 (reference count) = 0, rsi stored at +0x48, list-2 header self-linked (+0x18 = +0x20 = destination + 0x18). The +0x34 dword is not written.
phases.name: prologue field writes (unconditional, in instruction order)

phases.detail: if rdx == rdi the routine returns at once after the prologue (je at 0x5f12897 to the epilogue at 0x5f12948). The sole caller passes a fresh allocation, so the guard is not reachable from it; it is pinned as written.
phases.name: self-copy guard

phases.detail: if [source + 0x00] != source (list 1 nonempty): call the list-copy helper at 0x5f128b5 (contract above), which fills the destination list 1 with fresh nodes carrying the source payloads in order and raises +0x10 by the copied count; then walk the destination list 1 from [destination + 0x00] and addl-increment the dword at payload +0x70 of every node (wrapping modulo 2**32, no lock prefix). If the source list 1 is empty this phase is skipped entirely.
phases.name: list 1: deep copy, then payload bump

phases.detail: a lockstep walk overwrites destination list-2 nodes' +0x10 payload slots from the source list 2; if the source runs out first, a destroy loop decrements +0x28 per surplus destination node, unlinks it via _List_node_base::_M_unhook (PLT call at 0x5f1296f) and frees it via operator delete(node, 0x18) (PLT call at 0x5f1297c); if the destination runs out first, the helper call at 0x5f12924 deep-copies the remaining source range. The block ends by walking the whole destination list 2 and incrementing every node's payload +0x70 dword.
phases.name: list 2: reconciliation block, as written

phases.detail: the destination list-2 cursor for the reconciliation is [destination + 0x18], reloaded at 0x5f128bd after the list-1 helper call on the list-1 path, or the header value itself on the skipped-list-1 path (0x5f12988). The prologue self-linked that header and the helper writes only list 1 of the destination, so the cursor is always the header: the lockstep body never executes, the destroy loop never destroys, and any nodes linked into the destination list 2 before the call are orphaned by the prologue -- neither overwritten, bumped, unlinked nor freed. On every reachable run the helper deep-copies the entire source list 2 and the closing walk bumps the copies' payloads. Verified byte-for-byte against the model in the packet differential, including preloaded-destination cases.
phases.name: list 2: what is actually reachable
